newsitem.title: BULGARIA: U.S advisor warns Bulgaria on currency board delay.
newsitem.headline: U.S advisor warns Bulgaria on currency board delay.

text.p: Bulgaria should not delay introducing a restrictive monetary regime known as a currency board as part of vital reforms pledged earlier this year, a U.S. economy adviser said on Monday.

"I do not see reason to delay any further the introduction of the currency board. If something that was expected to be done in the first part of July is postponed, the impression is the reforms are going slower," U.S. money expert Steve Hanke told reporters.
"This is not a good start...you start to race fast, not slow," said Hanke,
Hanke, a professor of applied economics who helped revive Argentina's peso and reform currencies in Estonia and Lithuania, is advising President Petar Stoyanov on forming Bulgaria's currency board.

Under an International Monetary Fund agreement, Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a self-regulating mechanism where the amount of levs in circulation has to be fully covered by foreign exchange reserves.

Prime minister designate Ivan Kostov, said on Wednesday parliament will complete work on legal amendments needed to make the system operational by the end of July. He is expected to present his cabinet lineup to parliament on Wednesday.

Bulgaria's interim cabinet proposed on Monday to peg the lev to the mark as anchor currency hoping to boost investment from the European Union and harmonise its currency with the European Monetary Union to be set up in 1999.
Hanke said that the dollar, traditionaly perceived as benchmark of stability in Bulgaria, is preferable, mainly because Bulgarians are more familiar with it.
An International Monetary Fund mission is in Sofia to help draft legal amendments needed to make the board operational. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
